intro: Buying a home in Pennsylvania involves more than comparing mortgage rates and property prices. School district taxes, municipal levies, homeowners insurance and closing expenses can significantly influence how much you need to budget.

Our free Pennsylvania mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment before purchasing a property. Whether you're buying in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Allentown or a smaller Pennsylvania community, enter your financing details and ownership expenses to compare properties and establish a realistic purchase budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Pennsylvania?

blocks.markdown:
A $255,000 Pennsylvania home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,223.08.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or association fees. Property taxes, insurance premiums and the interest rate are illustrative rather than verified statewide averages.

Pennsylvania offers housing opportunities across major metropolitan areas, suburban neighborhoods, university communities and rural regions.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Pennsylvania housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/PA/HSG860223), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $254,500 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $1,762, while approximately 69.3% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures include existing homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions. They do not represent current property asking prices.

Housing expenses in suburban Philadelphia may differ considerably from those in western Pennsylvania or smaller central Pennsylvania communities.

Investigate recent comparable sales, school district taxes, transportation expenses and property maintenance requirements before entering a purchase price into the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the Pennsylvania Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter your property's expected purchase price and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Choose your preferred repayment period and enter your lender's quoted annual interest rate. If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, enter annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees where applicable.

Include private mortgage insurance if your conventional financing requires it.

Review your estimated monthly payment and experiment with different loan terms and down payment amounts.

The amortization schedule shows how your outstanding mortgage balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay.

Use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare financing scenarios outside Pennsylvania.

sections.heading: How Pennsylvania Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Pennsylvania property taxes are particularly important when comparing homes across different school districts.

County assessment systems determine property valuations, while municipalities, counties and school districts establish applicable real estate tax rates.

Your property's assessed value may differ considerably from its current purchase price because assessment practices and reassessment schedules vary between counties.

Obtain the property's taxable assessed value directly from the relevant county assessment office.

### Understanding Pennsylvania millage rates

A mill represents $1 of annual property tax for every $1,000 of taxable assessed value.

A property's combined millage rate may include separate county, municipal and school district components.

When reviewing tax records, make sure you account for all applicable tax bills rather than relying exclusively on one municipal charge.

### Pennsylvania property tax calculation example

Suppose you purchase a home for $255,000, but its taxable assessed value is $175,000.

Assume the following hypothetical millage rates.

The estimated annual property tax would be:

$175,000 × 24 ÷ 1,000 = $4,200

This represents approximately $350 per month.

Actual property taxes depend on local assessments, tax rates and applicable exclusions or additional charges.

Pennsylvania's Taxpayer Relief Act provides mechanisms for reducing property taxes on qualifying primary residences.

The [Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development's homestead exclusion guidance](https://dced.pa.gov/local-government/property-tax-relief-homestead-exclusion/) explains that eligible exclusions reduce assessed property value before applicable taxes are calculated.

The amount of relief varies by jurisdiction. Pennsylvania does not provide one universal homestead exclusion amount for every homeowner.

Applications for school property tax relief generally must be submitted to the county assessment office by March 1.

### Homestead exclusion calculation example

Suppose the property from our previous example qualifies for a hypothetical $20,000 exclusion applicable only to the school district tax component.

At a school district rate of 15 mills, the annual tax savings would be $300.

The estimated combined annual property tax would decrease from $4,200 to $3,900, equivalent to $325 per month.

Do not automatically apply a school district exclusion to county and municipal tax calculations.

Philadelphia also has distinct local relief arrangements. Confirm applicable programs with your local government rather than assuming every Pennsylvania municipality uses identical rules.

sections.heading: Pennsylvania Property Tax and Rent Rebate Program

blocks.markdown:
The [Pennsylvania Department of Revenue's Property Tax/Rent Rebate Program](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/ptrr) offers income-based assistance to qualifying older residents and people with eligible disabilities.

For claims concerning the 2025 tax year, the published income ceiling is $48,110, with standard rebates ranging from $380 to $1,000.

Some applicants may qualify for supplemental benefits.

These rebates are separate from ordinary homestead exclusions and should not automatically be subtracted from monthly mortgage escrow expenses.

Confirm eligibility and application requirements before incorporating expected benefits into your household budget.

Insurance premiums depend on your property's construction, condition, location, replacement cost and selected coverage.

Pennsylvania properties may experience heavy rainfall, flooding, winter storms and other weather-related damage.

### Flood insurance

The [Pennsylvania Insurance Department's flood insurance guidance](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/insurance/consumer-help-center/learn-about-insurance/flood-insurance) explains that standard homeowners policies exclude flood damage.

Properties near rivers, streams and low-lying communities may require additional coverage.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate flood exposure before obtaining insurance quotes.

### Insurance considerations for older homes

Older Pennsylvania properties may contain aging electrical systems, plumbing, roofing or heating equipment.

These conditions can influence insurance eligibility, repair expenses and premiums.

Arrange a professional home inspection before purchasing. Ask your insurer whether the property's condition affects available coverage or deductible requirements.

Include the combined annual premiums of applicable insurance policies when calculating monthly housing expenses.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete monthly payments, particularly when evaluating homes in different school districts.

The Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency, commonly called PHFA, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through approved lenders.

### Keystone Home Loan

The [PHFA home purchase programs directory](https://www.phfa.org/programs/homepurchase.aspx) includes Keystone Home Loan financing for qualifying first-time buyers.

Certain repeat buyers purchasing in targeted areas and eligible veterans may qualify for exceptions.

Household income, purchase price, occupancy and underwriting requirements apply.

### Keystone Forgivable in Ten Years

The [K-FIT assistance program](https://www.phfa.org/programs/assistance/kfit.aspx) provides qualifying borrowers with secondary financing equal to 5% of the lesser of the purchase price or appraised property value.

There is no maximum dollar cap on the assistance under this formula.

For example, a property purchased for $255,000 but appraised at $250,000 could qualify for $12,500 in assistance.

The loan is forgiven at a rate of 10% annually over ten years, subject to program conditions.

Applicants must have a minimum credit score of 660 and satisfy applicable first mortgage requirements.

### Keystone Due At Time of Expiration

PHFA also offers [K-DATE assistance](https://www.phfa.org/programs/assistance.aspx) through qualifying mortgage products.

Eligible borrowers with loan amounts of $150,000 or less may receive 8% assistance, subject to availability. Borrowers with loan amounts of $150,001 or more may receive 5%.

Both calculations use the lesser of the purchase price or appraised value.

K-DATE is an interest-free deferred second mortgage. It has no scheduled monthly payments, but repayment becomes due under specified conditions, including property sale, refinancing or repayment of the primary mortgage.

Compare the forgiveness and repayment arrangements before choosing an assistance program.

sections.heading: Pennsylvania Realty Transfer Tax and Closing Costs

blocks.markdown:
Pennsylvania imposes a state realty transfer tax of 1% on qualifying property transfers.

According to the [Pennsylvania Department of Revenue](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/resources/tax-types-and-information/realty-transfer-tax), additional local transfer taxes may also apply.

For a qualifying $255,000 property transfer, the state tax component would total $2,550 before local charges.

This does not necessarily represent the amount the buyer must pay individually. Both parties have statutory payment responsibilities, while the purchase agreement may allocate the expense between them.

Other closing costs include title services, appraisals, lender fees, inspections and prepaid expenses.

Review the [CFPB Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/) before accepting a mortgage offer.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Pennsylvania?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Use our [Pennsylvania Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/pennsylvania-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing borrowing commitments.

Include transportation, heating, utilities, childcare, maintenance and regular savings contributions.

Remember that local earned income taxes or wage taxes may also influence your available household income.

Maintain enough savings for closing expenses and emergency repairs instead of committing your entire cash balance to the down payment.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $255,000 Pennsylvania home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,223.08. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### How are Pennsylvania residential property taxes calculated?

Applicable county, municipal and school district tax rates are applied to the property's relevant taxable assessed value. Eligible homestead exclusions and other adjustments may reduce the final tax liability.

### Does Pennsylvania offer forgivable down payment assistance?

Yes. PHFA's K-FIT program provides eligible borrowers with assistance equal to 5% of the lesser of the purchase price or appraised value. The assistance is forgiven gradually over ten years, subject to program requirements.

Use our Pennsylvania mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, down payments, interest rates and repayment periods.

Replace illustrative property taxes and insurance premiums with verified local estimates. Pay particular attention to school district taxes, closing expenses and ongoing maintenance requirements when establishing a sustainable homebuying budget.
